ground_truth.text: The summary step runs under set -u and appends to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY with no fallback. On a runner that sets only <FORGE>_STEP_SUMMARY the variable is unbound, so a passing 'req diff' turns the step red.

github.base_ref is interpolated directly into the run script (req diff --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"), so a branch name containing $(cmd), backticks or ';' is command-substituted by the shell. It should arrive through env:.

The test for the job summary checks only the ordering of the write and the exit, not that the summary block holds the captured report and the exit status, so a template that drops the report from the summary would pass.
No test pins the workflow's token scope: nothing asserts permissions contents: read or the absence of any write scope for a job that runs on every pull request.

Neither the template nor docs/adopting.md says that a pull request from a fork has no repository secrets, so the install step refuses and the req-diff check is red on it; this behaviour is deliberate (trigger is pull_request, not pull_request_target) but undocumented.

findings.text: This prefix requires `jobs:` to immediately follow `on: pull_request:`, so it also rejects anything that does not affect the property under test — e.g. a top-level `permissions: { contents: read }` block (the recommended least-privilege placement, currently job-scoped in the workflow) or a `pull_request:` filter (`types:`/`paths:`/`branches:`). A security improvement or an ordinary PR filter would therefore turn this test red even though the trigger is still `pull_request` only. Consider asserting the `on:` block structurally (contains only `pull_request`, unknown triggers rejected) instead of a fixed textual prefix. Not a current failure: the workflow's `permissions:` is job-level, so this passes today.
findings.title: maintainability

findings.text: The test validates only the first `actions/checkout` step, so a second checkout added later without `fetch-depth: 0` would silently pass even though it would make the base revision unavailable. Iterate over every checkout occurrence and apply the same assertions to each.
findings.title: Validate every checkout step, not just the first

findings.text: This pair of sentences reads as contradictory for an adopter: `weakened` is put in the `--fail-on` set (so `req diff` exits 1 and, with a required check, blocks the merge), yet the next sentence says it is "not a rejection by req". The docs (`docs/adopting.md`) resolve this with the missing nuance -- loosening is sometimes right, and the point is that it is read on purpose. State that here, or adopters cannot tell whether `weakened` is advisory or blocking in the workflow they just copied.
findings.title: documentation

findings.text:
The workflow triggers on `pull_request`, but its install step requires
`secrets.REQ_RELEASE_TOKEN`. GitHub does not pass secrets (other than `GITHUB_TOKEN`)
to a workflow triggered by a pull request from a fork, so the install exits with
"REQ_RELEASE_TOKEN is not set" and the `req-diff` check is red for every external
contributor. The adopter section presents `--fail-on` as the merge gate, so a team that
marks this check required can never merge a fork PR. This may be the intended
trade-off, but neither the workflow header nor the new `## On a pull request` section
mentions it; document the limitation (and how to handle it) so adopters are not surprised.
findings.title: Fork PR failure

findings.text: The captured report file is created per run but never removed, so on a self-hosted runner each invocation leaks a temp file (the install step already cleans up its staging directory). Add an `EXIT` trap right after `mktemp` to remove it; the trailing `exit "$code"` still fires the trap and preserves the step's status.
findings.title: Clean up the captured report temp file

findings.text:
The step runs under `set -u` and appends with `>> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` without a
default. GitHub always sets that variable, but the file advertises itself as copyable to
`<removed forgejo workflow>`, and on a runner that does not set
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (some Forgejo/act_runner versions, or a local `act`) the
unbound-variable error aborts the shell after `req diff` has already run, so a passing
diff (exit 0) still fails the step. Using `>> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"` would
keep a missing summary from turning the check red (the pin test still matches the name).
I could not confirm whether current Forgejo/act_runner sets the variable, so treat this
as a robustness concern.
findings.title: Summary var unset

findings.text: The section is pinned for many prose claims but not for the exit-code contract that the whole workflow rests on: 0 = report produced, 1 = a `--fail-on` class/flag triggered, 3 = UNVERIFIABLE, 2 = usage error. Since the reason `fetch-depth: 0` matters is precisely that a shallow clone yields exit 3 (UNVERIFIABLE) rather than an empty report, a doc edit that drops that distinction (while keeping the `fetch-depth: 0` phrase) would still pass this test. Add a needle for the exit semantics — e.g. the `UNVERIFIABLE` wording / “cannot be produced” — so the doc keeps the three outcomes distinct.
findings.title: test

known_false.text: The OCR note that the workflow tests' pins are stricter than a hardening edit would allow.
known_false.why_refuted: Left as is: they are pins, strict by design.
